content_text: [1/2 @gregoryblotnick] on these other four, most of the slides are just too crowded to say that I'm a Temu version of the judges would be an insult to Temu but the first few pages gotta make it obvious to even an idiot 1. variance vs street on KPIs (quantitative) 2. few sentences on why (qualitative) THEN you can back all that up with the rest of the slides rather than having to flick around with everything dispersed or presented in the appendix PITCHES *EDIT: ADDED LINKS TO ALL FOUR PITCHES SIG https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6a74a44d44fa6357ee616596/t/6ae8b894f8f63239575d04cf/1793636500946/04_HighGamma_Short_SIG.pdf BROS https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6a74a44d44fa6357ee616596/t/6ae8b900413aa518f670721e/1793636608095/03_CreditCapital_Long_BROS.pdf ABNB https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6a74a44d44fa6357ee616596/t/6ae8b918ea4b3c13bd3203b0/1793636632479/02_NewLineCapital_Short_ABNB.pdf COCO https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6a74a44d44fa6357ee616596/t/6ae8b846c38ee41f00fe03c7/1793636422674/05_CavalierCapital_COCO.pdf --- 1. SIG: I can't figure out ests vs street aside from "we're 30% below on EPS"...this format has way too much going on, all these boxes everywhere, somewhere on page 6-7 I finally found the "SSS% vs street" box, and at the end a "KPI's vs. street," but there's probably 5-10 pages of filler that could be cut out (incl backward looking commentary) and/or reduced to tables more #'s, less words, always SIG PITCH: https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6a74a44d44fa6357ee616596/t/6ae8b894f8f63239575d04cf/1793636500946/04_HighGamma_Short_SIG.pdf 2. BROS: sort of the same problem, these slides are each overflowing with information (random slide here)... combining company data and consensus forecasts and model forecasts together on these pages makes it hard to answer 1. how many bps above/below are you on each kpi 2. what drives that like the charts/graphs where one line is "us" and another is "them" is vague to the point of not saying anything it isnt until Appendix F that kpi's vs street show up, I can't figure out what's extraneous but to have 19 overflowing pages, no pitch should be that complex, esp a coffee drive-thru 3. ABNB: I don't know the stock at all but this is much clearer to follow than the last two, I can see the few variables that matter + primary rsch + how everything is flexed and used to value the stock 4. COCO: this looks like "COCO trades 30x and we think its worth 20x" + this valuation page has a lot of assumptions that feel unreasonable page 3: "COCO currently trades at a 30x forward P/E and is expected to grow sales ~21% next year." then on valuation page: you have revenue growth of ~15%, flattish GM%, and then 220 bps of EBITDA margin downside (unclear why)... to get EPS 20% below street and the multiple goes from 30x to 20x the reasons listed don't seem extreme enough to justify that multiple compression + 20% EPS downside i.e. "We believe P/E will strongly rerate lower when growth slows and coconut commodity exposure becomes more visible to investors." I'm skeptical that a COCO bull is going to get railroaded by coconut commodity exposure + there's too much resting on weather, commodities, other "uncontrollables" that change daily (vs. a tenet like "impaired brand" which is much more powerful" but a lot of this falls under easily fixable i.e. your bull case / "Risk" EPS = 8% loss, vs 37% base gain and 60% bull gain soros had worse odds breaking the bank of england thats easy to adjust though, its just model monkey math, the biggest issues here are the translation of qualitative input to quantiative output and there are 27-28 year old megafund PE associates who would not be able to produce a pitch half this good great work all around --- [2/2 @gregoryblotnick] simplicity wins: https://x.com/gregoryblotnick/status/2117478254294503878?a=sRz1lXnG7_TPXMjur1k&s=20
